summary: Comprehensive backend regression for Monthly Touch OS. 40/40 pytest tests PASSED on the external preview URL covering: auth (bootstrap admin login, register, /me, role assignment, dup-email 409, no-token 401/403), dashboard overview (schema + auth guard), Clients CRUD (create/list/get/patch/delete with cascade verified via 404 on subsequent GET), Meetings CRUD, AI Brief generation (Claude Sonnet 4.6 — exactly 3 wins, 2 issues, talking_points, suggested_questions, strategic_recommendations, testimonial_opportunity, health_signal, kpi_snapshot persisted, status='prep'), AI Transcript analysis (real ~500-word transcript — sentiment correctly classified as 'positive', action_items + content_captures auto-created in MongoDB & verified via GET endpoints, client.sentiment + health_score updated), AI Recap (subject/html/plain returned), Action-Items list/patch/delete, Content-Captures list/patch (routed_to_marketing), Integrations catalog (13 platforms verified), Integrations status, configure→test→disconnect for clickup with encrypted credential storage (no secrets leaked in /api/integrations response — only configured_field_keys exposed), Docs list (>=14 docs incl. mtm-framework) + detail body + 404, AI models list (3 entries). Total runtime ~125s (AI endpoints took ~5-30s each).

minor.issue: When role is provided on registration, it is accepted from client input (data.role) for non-first users — any user can self-elevate to 'admin' via register payload. Should ignore role from public registration and only allow admin to create admin users.

Hard-deletes meeting but does NOT cascade-delete associated action_items / content_captures (only DELETE /api/clients/{id} does cascade). Could leave orphan rows referencing a non-existent meeting_id.

Accept raw dict payloads with no Pydantic validation — clients can write arbitrary fields (e.g., health_score=99999, role) directly into Mongo documents. Should use typed Pydantic patch models like MeetingPatch.
Any authenticated user (not just admin) can list every user incl. their emails and roles. Should be admin-only or scoped.
Return 200 with {ok:true} even when the resource does not exist (no 404). Inconsistent with /clients/{id} which 404s on GET but also silently succeeds on DELETE.

action_items: Harden POST /api/auth/register so role cannot be set by request body for non-first users (force role='manager' regardless of payload).
Replace untyped `patch: dict` parameters in PATCH client/action-item/content-capture handlers with explicit Pydantic patch models to prevent arbitrary field writes.
Cascade-delete action_items + content_captures when deleting a meeting (mirror /clients delete behavior).
Restrict GET /api/users to admin role only.
Return 404 on DELETE of missing resources for consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~610 lines — acceptable now but trending toward the 700 line guideline; consider splitting routers (auth, clients, meetings, integrations, docs) into separate modules.
Untyped `patch: dict` accepted by 3 PATCH endpoints — security & data-integrity risk; use Pydantic models.
`POST /api/auth/register` trusts client-supplied `role` field — privilege escalation vector.
`/api/users` lists all users to any authenticated caller — broaden access control.
Meeting deletion lacks cascade; orphan action_items/content_captures possible.

ai.py `_extract_json` is defensive but `_raw` is returned in response when parse succeeds (`None`) — fine; when it fails the entire response is degraded silently. Consider logging the raw on parse failure.
BaseDocument._id ObjectId handling — observed all responses use 'id' (string uuid via new_id) — _id is not leaking, good.
All endpoints properly use async/await; MongoDB queries are non-blocking — good.
Encrypted credentials via Fernet — verified secrets never leak to /api/integrations (only configured_field_keys exposed) — good.

seed_data_creation: Each test run creates a TEST_ prefixed client + meeting + action items + content captures; teardown tests delete the meeting and client (cascade deletes action_items / content_captures via client delete). Per-run TEST_ user is registered via /auth/register and not cleaned up (no delete user endpoint exists).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully green via /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — re-run with `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. AI tests (brief/analyze-transcript/recap) hit the real Emergent LLM key and take 5-30s each — keep AI_TIMEOUT >=90s. TEST_ prefix used for created data. Frontend has NOT been tested per the request scope. Mocked: KPI snapshot in /meetings/{id}/generate-brief is seeded demo data — that is by design and called out by the main agent.
